module_title: Most Famous National and Regional Festivals
introduction: India is known as the 'Land of Festivals'. Almost every state has its own unique festival, which is usually a celebration of the harvest season or the arrival of the regional New Year.

core_concepts.title: Pride of the North-East: Hornbill Festival
core_concepts.description:
State: **Nagaland**.
Key Feature: Widely known as the 'Festival of Festivals'. It is celebrated every year from December 1 to 10 at the 'Kisama Heritage Village' to showcase the rich culture of the Naga tribes. (It is named after the Hornbill bird).

core_concepts.title: South Indian Harvest Festivals: Onam & Pongal
core_concepts.description:
1. **Onam:** A 10-day harvest festival of **Kerala**. It is celebrated to commemorate the homecoming of the mythical King Mahabali. The famous snake boat race (Vallam Kali) takes place during this festival.
2. **Pongal:** A 4-day harvest festival of **Tamil Nadu** dedicated to the Sun God. The third day is 'Mattu Pongal', during which the famous and controversial bull-taming sport **'Jallikattu'** is played.

core_concepts.title: Kumbh Mela
core_concepts.description:
It is the largest peaceful religious gathering in the world. It is held once every 12 years at 4 specific locations:
1. **Prayagraj** (At the confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati)
2. **Haridwar** (River Ganga)
3. **Ujjain** (River Shipra)
4. **Nashik** (River Godavari)

important_entities.name: Lohri and Baisakhi
important_entities.significance: Lohri is celebrated in January (just before Makar Sankranti) to mark the end of winter. Baisakhi is celebrated on April 13/14 to mark the harvest of the Rabi crop and the historical founding of the Khalsa Panth.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
The Biggest Exam Trap: Students constantly mix up the states of these two major festivals under exam pressure. 
Remember strictly: Onam = Kerala. Pongal = Tamil Nadu.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
O-K = Onam (O) is in Kerala (K).
P-T = Pongal (P) is in Tamil Nadu (T).

exam_strategy_tips: The most repeated question in SSC CHSL/CGL: 'The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in which state of India?' Answer: Nagaland.
